2. Mr. Abdul Gani and Abdul Latif, who are the plaintiff-respondents in both the appeals, tiled Title Suit No. 26 of 1990, which on transfer was renumbered as Title Suit No. 22 of 1993, praying for declaration amongst others, that they are owners of 8 annas 4 gondas I kara and 2 kranties of land, which is equivalent to 62 decimals of land. In the plaint it was stated inter-alia that Abdul Hakim and Saijuddin, two brothers, were the owners of 11.61 acres of land in Khatian No. 29 which contained C.S. Plot No. 44 and then by amicable partition late Abdul Hakim, amongst others, got 1.21 acres of land in C.S. Plot No. 44, i.e. the suit plot, and after Abdul Hakim died. Halimon Bibi his 3rd wife, Rahatun Bibi, Suratun Nessa daughters through his first wife, Ismail and Nurbanu, his sons and daughter through his second wife and the plaintiffs, who are his sons through the above Halimon, his third wife, became owners of the suit land and that there had been no partition of the suit land amongst the heirs of Abdul Hakim either by amicable settlement or through Court. Then Halimun died leaving her 2 annas share in the suit land and thus each of the plaintiff got one anna share while the above heirs of Abdul Hakim were possessing the suit land in ejmali, the government acquired the same in L.A. Case No. 2 of 1987-88 and the defendant No. 4, who is entrusted with the duty of praying the amount of compensation against the above acquisition, after verifying the papers prepared the award in the names of the plaintiffs against acquisition of .62 acres of land out of 1.21 acres of land as contained in C.S. Plot No. 44 and issued notice dated 24.12.89 upon them under Section 7(3) of Ordinance, 1982 and after receiving the aforesaid notice, the plaintiffs went to the office of the defendant No. 4 but came to know that the defendant No. 1 lodged claim for compensation for the entire 1.21 acres of land of C.S. Plot No. 44 and then the plaintiff requested the defendant No. 4 for initiating a miscellaneous case to ascertain the shares of the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 in the amount of compensation payable against acquisition but the defendant No. 4 did not initiate the miscellaneous case and the defendant No. 1 is trying to withdraw the entire compensation money and if the defendant No. 1 succeeded in withdrawing the entire compensation amount, the plaintiff would suffer irreparable loss and injury. 

 4. The appellants, who are the defendants in the above Title Suit No. 22 of 1993 contested the suit and filed written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and stating inter alia that the suit is not maintainable as no consequential relief was sought and the suit is also barred by limitation and further the defendants also acquired title in the suit land by adverse possession and they also contested. Title Suit No. 13 of 1994 and filed written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and stating inter alia that the heirs of Abdul Hakim by Sale Deed No. 4512 dated 8.12.45 out of 1.21 acres of land, sold .62 acres of land to Zafar Ali, the father of defendant Nos. 1-3, and by sale deed No. 4513 executed on them the same day also sold the balance .59 acres of land in to Babar Ali, son of Wahed Ali, and thereby the right of title and interest of the heirs of late Abdul Hakim in the entire suit extinguished and subsequently by sale deed dated 9.12.47 Babor Ali sold the above .59 acres of land to Zafar Ali and thus Zafar All possessed 1.21 acres of land on the basis of the said sale deeds and also adversely and thereafter during S.A. operation the name of Zafar All was duly recorded in the S.A. Khatian. 

 13. Ext. 1 is the Parcha of C.S. Khatian No. 29 and Ext. 2 is the notice dated 24.12.89 under Section 7(3) of Ordinance 1982 asking the plaintiff to receive the compensation amount of Tk. 9,06,072.90 from the defendant No. 4. On the other hand the defendant in para 17(ka) of the written statement stated that by sale deed No. 4512 dated 8.12.45 the sons and daughters of Late Abdul Hakim sold .62 acres of land to Zafar Ali and they by Sale Deed No. 4513 dated 8.12.45 also sold .59 acres of land to Babar Ali and then by Sale Deed dated 9.12.74 Babar All sold said .59 acres of land to Zafar Ali and thus Zafar Ali became owner in possession of the entire 1.21 acres of land and in the aforesaid paragraph it was also stated that “এই ভাবে জাফর আলী নালিশী সি এস ৪৪ দাগের ১.২০ শতাংশ ভূমির মালিক দথলকারী সত্বাধিকারী এবং অন্যের বিরুদ্ধে দখল জনিত স্বত্বে ভোগ দখল করিতে রহেন ও থাকেন।”  So the submission of Mr. Alam that the defendants, in their pleading did not specifically pleaded acquiring of title by adverse possession are not correct. 

 15. In support of their claim of acquisition of title in the suit land by adverse possession, the defendants filed Ext. Ka, the C.S. Khatian No. 29 Ext.- Ka & Kha(1)2 Sale Deeds dated 8.12.45. Ext. Ga the Sale Deed dated 9.12.47. Ext Gha-Gha(2) i.e. the S.A. Khatians, Ext. Uma and Uma(1)2 Sale Deeds dated 18.3.78. Ext. Cha(2) notice dated 26.11.89 issued upon the predecessor of defendants under Section 7(3) of Ordinance 1982. Ext. Cha and Cha(1) are the Deeds of Indemnity by which the heirs of Abdul Hakim undertook to compensate Zafar All in case of any claim lodged by the minors, whose proper-ties were also sold by the aforesaid Deeds. Out of those, Exts. Gha, Gha(1) and Gha(2) S.A. Khatians shows that the name of Zafar Ali was recorded in the S.A. Khatian No. 49 formerly C.S. Khatian No. 29/1 and the names of Rajab Ali and Mansur Ali, who are son of Zafar Ali, were printed in R.S. Dag No. 402 and 414 which contained .62 and .59 of acres of land respectively, total of which 1.21 acres of land, and that defendant No. 1 got his name mutately in the suit land by Mutation Case No. 6453 dated 31.3.79.
